translations.text: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, along with some of the vessels of the house of the Lord. They carried him off to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and he brought the vessels into the house of his god.
And the king told Astophanes, his chief eunuch, to bring in some of the sons of the captives of Israel, from the royal family,

young men from among the captives who had no blemish, very handsome, understanding in all wisdom, possessing knowledge, discerning in understanding, and having the ability to stand in the king's house, so that they might learn the writing and the language of the Chaldeans.
And he assigned them a daily ration from his own table and from the wine he drank, so that they would be brought up for three years, and after that they would stand before the king.
And among them, of the sons of Judah, were Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael.
And the chief eunuch gave them names: to Daniel, Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Azariah, Meshach; to Mishael, Abednego.
And Daniel resolved in his heart not to defile himself with the royal table or with the wine he drank, and he begged the chief eunuch that he might not defile himself.
And God gave Daniel mercy and favour before the chief eunuch.

And the chief eunuch said to Daniel, "I am afraid of my lord the king, who has assigned you your food and drink. What if he sees your faces looking sadder than the faces of the young men who are your equals in age? Then I would be sentenced to death by the king."
And Daniel said to Amelsad, whom the chief eunuch had set over Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael:
"Test your servants for just ten days. Let them give us seeds of the earth to eat and water to drink.
Then let our faces and the faces of the young men who eat from the royal table be examined before you, and deal with your servants according to what you see."
And he listened to them and tested them for just ten days.
And at the end of the ten days their faces looked better and they were stronger in body than the young men who ate from the royal table.
And from then on Amelsad took away their food and the wine they were to drink, and gave them seeds.
And to these four young men God gave understanding and insight in all learning and wisdom, and Daniel understood everything, and visions.
At the end of those days the king ordered them to be brought before him, and the chief eunuch brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.
And the king spoke with them, and among them all no one was found like or equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael, and they stood before the king.
And in every matter of wisdom, speech and knowledge that the king asked of them, he found them ten times better than all the enchanters [?] and magi who were in his kingdom.
And Daniel remained until the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians.
In the second year of his reign King Nebuchadnezzar saw a vision. His spirit was troubled by the vision, and his sleep left him.
The king ordered that the magi, the enchanters and the sorcerers be summoned, so that they could tell the king his vision. They came and stood before the king.
The king said to them, "I have seen a vision, and my spirit is troubled to know what the vision was."
Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Syriac: "O king, live forever! Tell your vision to your servants, and we will tell you its interpretation."

The king answered the Chaldeans and said, "The matter has gone from me. If you do not make my vision known to me and tell me its interpretation, you will be handed over to destruction, and your houses will be plundered.
If you tell me my vision and its interpretation, you will receive gifts, honour and a great reward from me. Only tell me my vision and its interpretation."
They answered the king a second time: "Let the king tell his vision to his servants, and we will tell you its interpretation."
The king answered and said to them, "I know for certain that you are trying to gain time, because you have seen that the matter has gone from me.

If you do not tell me the vision, I know that you have agreed among yourselves to speak a lying and corrupt word before me until the time passes. Tell me my vision, and then I will know that you can also tell me its interpretation."
The Chaldeans answered the king again: "There is no man on earth who can tell the king this matter. No great king or ruler asks such a thing of any soothsayer, magus or Chaldean.
What the king asks is a hard thing. There is no one else who can tell it to the king except the gods, whose dwelling is not with any flesh."
Then the king, in anger and wrath, ordered the destruction of all the wise men of Babylon.
The decree went out and the wise men were being killed, and Daniel and his companions were also to be killed.
Then Daniel answered with counsel and understanding to Arioch, the king's chief eunuch, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
He asked him, "O chief officer of the king, why has this evil decree gone out from the king?" Then Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.
Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time, so that he could tell the king the interpretation of the vision.
Daniel went to his house and told the matter to his companions Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael.
They asked the God of heaven for mercy concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his companions would not be destroyed with the other wise men of Babylon.
Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night, and Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
He said, "Blessed be the name of the Lord from everlasting to everlasting, for wisdom and understanding are his.
He changes times and years. He sets up kings and removes them. He gives wisdom to the wise and prudence to those who have understanding.
He reveals deep things and knows what is hidden in darkness, and light is with him.
You, O God of our fathers, I confess and praise, for you have given me wisdom and power, and you have revealed to me what I asked of you, and you have made known to me the king's vision.

And Daniel came to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and said to him: "Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon, but bring me in before the king, and I will tell the king the interpretation of the vision."

Then Arioch quickly brought Daniel in before the king and said to him: "I have found a man from among the captives of the sons of Israel from Judea who will tell the king the interpretation of the visions."
The king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar: "Are you able to tell the vision that I saw, and its interpretation?"
Daniel answered before the king and said: "The mystery that the king asks about is not for the wise men, the magi, the diviners and the Gazarenes to tell the king;
but there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and he has revealed to King Nebuchadnezzar what is to happen in the last days.

Your dream and the vision of your head upon your bed is this, O king: your thoughts came to you upon your bed about what is to happen after this, and he who reveals mysteries has made known to you what is to happen.

And as for me, this mystery was revealed to me not by any wisdom that is in me more than in all living beings, but so that the interpretation of the visions might be made known to the king, so that you might know the thoughts of your heart.
You, O king, were watching, and behold, a great image; that image and its appearance were extraordinary. It stood before you, and its appearance was terrifying.
As for the image, its head was of pure gold; its hands and breast and arms were of silver; its belly and thighs were of bronze;
and its legs were of iron. Its feet were partly of iron and partly of clay.
You watched until a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands; it struck the image on its feet of iron and clay and crushed them completely.

And then the iron and the clay and the bronze and the silver and the gold were crushed together, and they became like the chaff of a threshing floor in summer, and the force of the wind carried it away, and no place at all was found for them. And the stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
This is the vision, and we shall also tell its interpretation before the king.
You, O king, are the king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given a kingdom mighty, strong and honoured.

In every place where the sons of men dwell, he has given into your hand the beasts of the field, the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, and he has set you as lord over them all. You are that head of gold.
And after you there will arise another kingdom inferior to yours, and a third kingdom, which is the bronze, which will rule over all the earth.
And the fourth kingdom will be strong like iron; and just as iron crushes and subdues everything on the earth, so it will crush and subdue all.
And as you saw the feet and the toes, partly of iron and partly of clay, the kingdom will be divided, and some of the root of the iron will be in it, just as you saw the iron mixed with the clay.
And the toes of the feet were partly of iron and partly of clay: part of that kingdom will be strong, and part of it will in turn be broken,
for you saw iron mixed with clay: they will be mingled by the seed of men, but they will not be joined one with another, just as iron does not unite with clay.

And in the days of those kings the God of heaven will raise up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, and his kingdom will not be made subject to another people. It will crush and destroy every kingdom of the earth, and it will stand forever.

Just as you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without a hand, and it crushed the clay and the iron and the bronze and the silver and the gold, so the great God has revealed to the king what is to come hereafter. The vision is true, and its interpretation is trustworthy.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and worshipped Daniel, and offered an offering and incense to him.
And the king answered and said to Daniel, "Truly your God is himself the God of gods and Lord of lords and King of kingdoms. He reveals mysteries, for you were able to make this mystery known to me."
And the king exalted Daniel and gave him great and many gifts, and set him over the whole province of Babylon, and made him chief of the prefects, and set him over all the wise men of Babylon.
And Daniel asked the king for Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, and he appointed them over the affairs of the province of Babylon; and Daniel remained at the king's court.
In the eighteenth year King Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold. Its height was sixty cubits and its breadth six cubits, and he set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

And he sent to gather the satraps, the governors, the provincial rulers, the notables, the mighty, the men of authority, and all the rulers of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the idol that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

And the satraps, the governors, the notables, the mighty, the great men of authority, and all the rulers gathered for the dedication of the idol that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood before the idol.
And a herald cried out loudly: "To you I say, peoples, tribes and languages:

At the moment you hear the sound of the horn, the pipe, the flute, the lyre, the psaltery, the music, and every kind of music, you shall fall down and worship the image that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
And whoever does not fall down and worship shall at that very hour be cast into the furnace of blazing fire."

And so, when the people heard the sound of the horn, the flute, the lyre, the psaltery, the music, the singing, and every kind of music, all the tribes and languages fell down and worshipped the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Then some Chaldean men came forward and accused the Jews
to King Nebuchadnezzar. They said to him, "O king, live forever!
You, O king, laid down a decree that every man who hears the sound of the flute, the horn, the lyre, the psaltery and the music
and does not fall down and worship the golden image shall be cast into the furnace of blazing fire.

There are Jewish men whom you have appointed over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, who have not obeyed your command, O king. They do not serve your gods, and they do not bow down to the golden image that you set up.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar, in furious anger, commanded that Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego be brought, and they brought these men before the king.
King Nebuchadnezzar answered and said to them: "Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods and do not bow down to the golden image that I set up?

Now, if you are ready, when you hear the sound of the horn, the pipe, the lyre, the harp, the music and the singing, and every kind of music, fall down and bow down to the golden image that I set up. If you do not bow down, at that very hour you will be thrown into the furnace of blazing fire. And who is the god who will deliver you out of my hand?"
Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego answered and said to King Nebuchadnezzar: "We have no need to give you an answer about this matter,
for there is a God whom we serve, and he is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire, and he will rescue us from your hands too, O king.
But if not, let it be known to you that we will not serve your gods, and we will not bow down to the golden idol that you set up."
Then King Nebuchadnezzar was filled with anger, and the look of his face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, and he said: "Heat that furnace sevenfold, until it blazes fully."
And he told strong, mighty men to bind Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego and to throw them into the furnace of blazing fire.

Then these men were bound together with their trousers and tunics, their turbans and their leggings, and all their clothing, and they were thrown, bound, into the midst of the furnace of blazing fire.
For the king's command was urgent, and the furnace of fire was heated exceedingly, and the flame all around killed the men who threw in Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego.
And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, were thrown bound into the midst of the furnace of blazing fire.
And they walked in the midst of the flame of fire, singing praise to God and blessing the Lord.
And Azariah stood up and prayed thus; he opened his mouth in the midst of the fire and said:
"Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our fathers, and your name is praised and glorified forever.
For you are just in all that you have done to us, and all your works are true, and your ways are upright, and all your judgment is true.

And you have brought a righteous judgment upon us, for all that you have brought upon us, for all that you have done to us, and upon the holy city of our fathers, Jerusalem; for by true judgment you have done all this to us because of our sins.
For we have sinned against you and have done lawlessness in everything.
And we did not obey your commandments, nor did we keep them, nor did we do as you commanded us, so that it might go well with us.
And all that you have brought upon us, and all that you have done to us, you have done by true judgment.
And you have handed us over to our enemies: lawless, harsh rebels, and a lying king who is more wicked than anyone on all the earth.
And now we cannot open our mouths, because shame and disgrace have come upon your servants and those who worship you.
Do not hand us over completely, for your name's sake. Do not cancel your covenant,
and do not take your mercy away from us, for the sake of Abraham your beloved, Isaac your servant, and Israel your holy one,
to whom you spoke and said: "I will multiply your descendants like the stars of the sky and like the sand on the seashore."
And now, Lord, we have become fewer than any of the nations, and today we are brought low in all the earth because of our sins.
At this time there is no ruler, prophet or leader, no holy offering [?], no sacrifice, no oblation, no incense, and no place to offer fruit before you and to find mercy.
But with a humbled head and a lowly spirit may we be accepted as an offering,

as if we were whole burnt offerings of rams and bulls, and tens of thousands of fat lambs. So let this sacrifice of ours be offered before you today, so that we may follow you wholeheartedly, and so that none of those who trust in you may be put to shame.
Now we have set out on your path to follow you with all our heart. We fear you, and we seek your face, Lord.
Do not put us to shame. Instead, show us your mercy in your kindness and in your great mercy.
Rescue us by your wonders, and bring glory to your name, Lord,
so that all who do evil to your servants may be put to shame. Let their tyranny be disgraced, and let all their strength be crushed,
and let them know that you alone are the Lord God over the whole world.
And the king's servants who had thrown the three young men in did not stop feeding the furnace with naphtha, pitch, tow and vine cuttings.
And the flame rose forty-nine cubits above the furnace.
It spread out and burned all the Chaldeans it found around the furnace.
But the angel of the Lord came down among Azariah and his companions and drove the flames of fire out of the furnace.
He made the inside of the furnace like a whistling wind full of dew, and the fire did not touch them at all. It neither troubled them nor harmed them in any way.
Then the three of them, as if with one mouth, sang hymns to God in the furnace, blessing and glorifying him, and said:
Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers, praised and glorified and exalted forever. Blessed is the holy name of your glory, praised, glorified and exalted forever.
Blessed are you in the holy temple of your glory, praised, glorified and exalted forever.
Blessed are you who sit upon the cherubim and look into the depths, praised, glorified and exalted forever.
Blessed are you on the thrones of your kingdom, praised, glorified and exalted forever.
Blessed are you above the firmament, in the heaven of heavens, praised, glorified, blessed and exalted above all forever.
Bless the Lord, all you works of the Lord; sing praise to him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, you heavens.
Bless the Lord, you angels.
Bless the Lord, all you waters above the heavens.
Bless the Lord, sun and moon.
Bless the Lord, you stars of heaven.
Bless the Lord, every rain and dew.
Bless the Lord, all you winds.
Bless the Lord, fire and heat.
Bless the Lord, nights and days.
Bless the Lord, light and darkness.
Bless the Lord, cold and warmth.
Bless the Lord, frost and snow.
Bless the Lord, lightnings and clouds.
Bless the Lord, O earth.
Bless the Lord, mountains and hills.
Bless the Lord, every plant of the earth.
Bless the Lord, sea and rivers.
Bless the Lord, you springs.
Bless the Lord, you sea monsters and all that move in the waters.
Bless the Lord, all you birds of the sky.
Bless the Lord, you wild beasts and all cattle.
Bless the Lord, you children of men.
Bless the Lord, O Israel.
Bless the Lord, you priests of the Lord.
Bless the Lord, you servants of the Lord.
Bless the Lord, you spirits and souls of the righteous.
Bless the Lord, you holy ones and you who are humble of heart.

Bless the Lord, Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael; sing praise to him and exalt him for ever. For he has rescued us from Hell and saved us from the hand of death, and delivered us from the midst of the furnace of fire and flame, and from the midst of the fire he has set us free.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is gracious, for his mercy endures for ever.
Bless the Lord, all you who serve the Lord. Sing praise to the God of gods and give thanks to him, for his mercy endures for ever.

When Nebuchadnezzar heard their singing, he was amazed, and he came in haste to the door of the furnace. He called his nobles and said to them, "Did we not cast three men, bound hand and foot, into the midst of the furnace?" They answered and said, "[?] O king."

And the king said, "Then what is this that I see: four men, loose of foot and loose of hand, who have gone in and are walking about [?] in the midst of that furnace, and no harm is on them, and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of God."
Then Nebuchadnezzar went up to the door of the furnace of blazing fire and said, "Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, you servants of the Most High God, come out of that furnace, out of the fire."

And the princes, the governors, the rulers of the land and the mighty men of the people, as many as belonged to the king, gathered together and looked at those men: the fire had had no power over their bodies, the hair of their heads was not singed, their clothing was not harmed, and there was no smell of fire on them at all.

And Nebuchadnezzar answered and said, "Blessed is the Lord, the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, who sent his angel and delivered his servants, because they trusted in him. They set the king's word at nought and gave their bodies to the fire, so that they would not serve or worship any other god but their own God alone.

"And I issue a decree that every people, nation and language that speaks blasphemy against the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego shall be given over to destruction, and their houses shall be cut down, because there is no other god who can deliver in this way."
Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the land of the Babylonians, and honoured them as leaders over all the Jews who were under his kingdom.
I, King Nebuchadnezzar, to all peoples, nations and languages that dwell in all the earth: may your peace be multiplied.
The signs and wonders that the Most High God has worked with me, it has seemed good to me to recount to you,
how great and mighty they are. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his dominion is from generation to generation.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house, and like a fine plant over my people.
I saw a vision and I was afraid; I trembled upon my bed, and the vision of my head terrified me.
And I issued a decree that all the wise men be brought in before me, so that they might tell us the interpretation of the dream.
All the wise men, the magi and the Chaldeans, had come in and were standing before me. I told them the dream, and they could not tell me its interpretation,

until Daniel came in, who is called Belteshazzar after the name of my god, for the holy spirit of his God is with him; the chief called him Belteshazzar. Of you I know and am aware that the holy spirit is with you,
and no secret thing is hidden from you. Now hear the vision of my dream, and tell me its interpretation concerning the people [?].
There was a tree standing in the midst of the earth, and its height was very great.
It grew tall, it swelled up [?], it reached up to the clouds of heaven, and it spread out and filled all the ends of the earth.

Its leaves were beautiful and its fruit was abundant, and in it was food for all. All the beasts of the field camped beneath it, all the birds of heaven dwelt in its branches, and all flesh was nourished from it.
I was seeing a vision of the night upon my bed, and behold, a holy watcher came down from heaven,

and he cried out with power and said this: Cut down that tree and lop off its branches, strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the beasts be driven from under it, and the birds from its branches.

But leave only the shoot of its roots. Let him lie down bound with a fetter of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field and with the dew of heaven. Let his portion be with the beasts of the field, and let him eat the grass of the earth.
Let his heart be changed from that of men, let the heart of a beast be given to him, and let seven times pass over him.

The word is by the decree of the watcher, and the question is the saying of the holy ones, so that those who are living may know that the Lord Most High rules over the kingdom of men. He gives it to whomever he wills, and he sets the despised among men over it.

This is the vision that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. Belteshazzar, tell me its interpretation, for all the wise men of my kingdom were not able to make its interpretation known to me. But you are able, for the holy spirit of God is with you.

Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was astounded for about one hour, and his thoughts troubled him. The king answered and said to him: Belteshazzar, do not let the vision and its interpretation alarm you. But Belteshazzar said to him: O king, may this vision be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies.
The tree that you saw grew great and strong. Its height reached up to heaven, and its breadth reached over all the earth.
Its leaves were beautiful and its fruit was abundant, and in it was food for all. The beasts of the field dwelt beneath it, and the birds of heaven dwelt in its branches.
You are that tree, O king, for you have grown great and strong. Your wealth has grown great and reached to heaven, and your dominion reaches to the ends of the earth.

O king, you saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven, and he said: Lop off the branches of the tree and destroy it, but leave only the shoot of its roots in the earth. Let him live bound with a bond of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field and with the dew of heaven, and let his portion be with the beasts of the field until seven times pass over him.
This is its interpretation, O king, and this interpretation is from the Most High, and it has come upon my lord the king.

They will drive you out from among men, and your dwelling will be with the wild beasts of the field. They will feed you grass like an ox, and you will live under the dew of heaven. Seven times will pass over you until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of men and gives it to whomever he wishes.
And because he said, "Leave the shoot of the roots of that tree," your kingdom will wait for you until you know the dominion of heaven.
Therefore, O king, let my counsel be pleasing to you: redeem your sins by acts of charity, and your iniquities by mercy to the poor. Who knows whether there may yet be patience for your sins?
All this came upon Nebuchadnezzar.
After twelve months he was walking about in the royal palace in Babylon.
He spoke up and said, "Is this not great Babylon, which I built as a royal house by the might of my power, for the honor of my glory?"
While the word was still in the king's mouth, a voice came down from heaven and said, "To you it is said, Nebuchadnezzar: your kingdom has departed from you.

They will drive you out from among men, and your dwelling will be with the wild beasts of the field. They will feed you grass like an ox, and seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of men and gives it to whomever he wishes."

At that very hour it was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven out from among men and ate grass like an ox, and his body was soaked with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like a lion's and his nails like a bird's.

At the end of those days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my understanding was given back to me. I blessed the Most High, and I praised and glorified him who lives forever, for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his reign is from generation to generation.

All the inhabitants of the earth are counted as nothing. He does according to his own will with the host of heaven and with the inhabitants of the earth. There is no one who can stand against his power and say to him, "What is this you have done?"

At that time my understanding returned to me, and I came back to the honor of my reign, and the color of my beauty returned to me. My mighty men and my great nobles sought me out, I was established over my kingdom, and still greater glory was given to me.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, for all his works are true and his ways are just, and he is able to humble all who walk in pride.
King Belshazzar made a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and drank wine before the thousand.
While Belshazzar was drinking and tasting the wine, he ordered that the vessels of gold and silver be brought, which Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken out of the temple in Jerusalem.
And the king, his nobles, his concubines and his attendants drank from them.
They drank wine and praised idols of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone.

At that hour the hand of a man appeared, with its fingers, and it wrote opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the king's house. And the king saw the hand with its fingers that was writing.
Then the appearance of the king's face changed, and his thoughts terrified him. The joints of his loins were loosened, and his knees knocked together.

And the king cried out loudly and ordered that the magi and the Chaldeans and the diviners (gazarenes) be brought in. And he said to the wise men of Babylon, "Whoever reads this writing and makes its interpretation known to me shall be clothed in purple, with a chain of gold on his neck, and he shall rule as third in my kingdom."
And all the king's wise men came in, but they could not read the writing, nor could they make its interpretation known to the king.
And King Belshazzar was terrified, and the color of his face kept changing, and his nobles trembled along with him.
And the queen came into the house where they were drinking, and she said, "O king, live forever! Do not let your thoughts terrify you, and do not let the color of your face change.

There is a man in your kingdom in whom is the holy spirit of God. In the days of your father, watchfulness and understanding were found in him. And King Nebuchadnezzar, your father, appointed him chief of the enchanters [?], the magi, the diviners and the Chaldeans,

because a surpassing spirit was found in him, and prudence and understanding. Daniel declared all of this: the interpretation of visions and the telling of hidden things, and also the loosing of knots. And the king gave him the name Belteshazzar. Now summon him, and he will tell you its interpretation."
Then Daniel was brought in before the king, and the king said to Daniel, "Are you Daniel, one of the sons of the captivity of Judea, whom King Nebuchadnezzar, my father, brought here?
I have heard about you that the holy spirit of God is in you, and that watchfulness and understanding and surpassing wisdom have been found in you.
Now the wise men, the magi, the diviners and the Chaldeans came in before me to read this writing and tell me its interpretation, but they were not able to explain it to me.

And I have heard about you that you interpret judgments. Now if you are able to read this writing and explain its interpretation to me, you shall be clothed in purple, with a chain of gold on your neck, and you shall rule as third in my kingdom."
And Daniel said before the king, "Keep your gift, and give the rewards of your house to another. But I will read that writing and make its interpretation known to you.
O king, God Most High gave kingship and greatness and honor to Nebuchadnezzar your father.

And because of the greatness that God gave him, all peoples, tribes and tongues trembled and were afraid before him. Whomever he wished, he killed; whomever he wished to torment, he tormented; whomever he wished, he exalted; and whomever he wished, he humbled.
And when his heart was lifted up and his spirit grew arrogant, he was cast down from his kingship and from his throne, and his honor was taken from him,

And he was driven out from among people, and the heart of a beast was given to him, and his dwelling was with the wild asses. They fed him grass like an ox, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, until he knew that God Most High rules over the kingdom of humans and gives it to whomever he wishes.
And you, his son Belshazzar, did not humble your heart before God, though you knew all this.

You exalted yourself against the Lord God of heaven, and you had the vessels of his temple brought before you, and you and your nobles, your concubines and your wives drank wine from them. And you praised idols of gold and silver, of bronze and iron, of wood and stone, which do not see, do not hear and know nothing. But your God, in whose hand are your breath and all your ways, you forgot and did not glorify.
Therefore this human hand was sent from his presence, and it set down this writing.
And this is the writing that was set down: Mene, Tekel, Parsin.
And this is the interpretation of the word. Mene: God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end.
Tekel: it has been weighed in the balance and found wanting.
Parsin: your kingdom has been divided and given to the Medes and the Persians.
And Belshazzar gave the order, and they clothed Daniel in purple and put a gold chain around his neck, and he sent out the herald concerning him, that he should be third in his kingdom.
That night Belshazzar the Chaldean was killed.
And Darius the Mede received the kingdom; he was sixty-two years old.
And it seemed good to him, and he appointed over his kingdom a hundred and twenty officials, to be over his kingdom.
And over them were three others who were appointed, and Daniel was one of them, so that the officials would give account to them and the king would not be burdened by anything.
And Daniel was greater than them, because a surpassing spirit was in him, and the king appointed him over his whole kingdom.
And the appointed overseers and the officials sought to find some grounds against Daniel, but they found no grounds, no wrongdoing and no fault in him, because Daniel was faithful.
And the overseers said, "We have not found any grounds against Daniel except in the law of his God."
Then the overseers and the officials came to the king and said to him, "King Darius, live forever!

All the governors of your realm, the rulers of the lands, the marzpans and the nakhapets, have consulted together to establish a royal statute and to enforce a decree, that whoever makes a petition to any god or man for thirty days, except to you alone, O king, shall be thrown into the lions' den.
Now, O king, establish the decree and send out the documents, so that the decree of the Medes and the Persians may not be changed."
Then King Darius ordered this law to be written. And when Daniel heard that he had written this decree,
he went into his house, and his windows were open in his upper room toward Jerusalem, and three times a day he would kneel down, pray and give thanks to his God, as he had done before.
Then those men spied on him, and they found Daniel making supplication and praying to his God.

And they came and said to the king: "Did you not lay down a decree that any man who makes a petition to any god or man for thirty days, except to you alone, O king, should be thrown into the pit of lions?" And the king said: "The word is true, and the decree of the Medes and Persians shall not pass away."
Then they answered and said before the king: "Daniel, one of the sons of the captivity of Judea, has not obeyed your decree, O king, and three times a day he makes petition to his God."
Then, when the king heard these words, he was greatly distressed over Daniel, and he strove for him so as to deliver him, and until evening he was in struggle so that he might deliver him.
Then those men said to the king: "Know, O king, that the decree of the Medes and Persians, and any ordinance and rule that the king establishes, must not be changed."
Then the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the pit of lions. And the king said to Daniel: "May your God, whom you serve continually, deliver you."

And they brought a stone and laid it on the mouth of the pit, and the king sealed it with his own seal and with the seal of his nobles, so that nothing might be changed in the matter concerning Daniel.
And the king went to his house and lay down without supper, and he asked for no food, and sleep departed from him. And God shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not touch Daniel.
Then the king rose very early at dawn and went in haste to the pit of lions.
And when he reached the pit, he cried out with a loud voice and said: "Daniel, servant of the living God, has the God whom you serve continually been able to deliver you from the mouth of the lions?"
And Daniel said to the king: "O king, live forever!
My God sent his angel and stopped the mouths of the lions, and they did not devour me, because my innocence was found before him; and before you also, O king, I had committed no offense."
Then the king rejoiced over him and ordered that Daniel be brought up out of the pit. And they brought Daniel up out of the pit, and no harm was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

And the king gave orders, and they brought those men who had accused Daniel, and they threw them into the pit of lions, them and their sons and their wives. And before they had even reached the floor of the pit, the lions overpowered them and crushed and ground all their bones to pieces.
Then King Darius wrote to all peoples, tribes, and languages: "You who dwell in all the earth, may peace be multiplied upon you.

From me a decree has been laid down to all the provinces of my kingdom, that they should fear and tremble before the God of Daniel, for he is the living God and endures forever, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed, and his dominion is to the end.
He helps and delivers, and he works signs and wonders in heaven and on earth, he who delivered Daniel from the mouth of the lions."
And Daniel prospered in the reign of King Darius and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
In the first year of Belshazzar, king of the Chaldeans, Daniel saw a dream, and the visions of his head upon his bed, and he wrote down the dream.
I, Daniel, was watching, and behold, the four winds of heaven came upon the great sea,
and four beasts were coming up out of the sea, each one greater than the other, differing from one another.

The first was like a lioness, and it had wings like an eagle's. I watched until its wings were plucked off, and it was lifted up from the earth and stood on feet like a man's, and a man's heart was given to it.
And behold, a second beast, like a bear, and it raised itself up on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth, and they said to it, "Arise, and eat the flesh of many."
After this I watched, and behold, another beast, like a leopard, and it had four wings of a bird on its back, and the beast had four heads, and authority was given to it.

And after this I saw, and behold, the fourth beast, terrible and dreadful, mightier than the former ones; its [?] (teeth?) were of iron and great. It devoured everything and crushed it to pieces, and trampled the remainder with its feet. It was greater than all, far beyond the other beasts that came before it, and it had ten horns.

I was considering its horns, and behold, another small horn was coming up among them, and three of the earlier horns were plucked out before it. And behold, there were eyes like a man's eyes in that horn, and a mouth that spoke great things, and it made war against the saints.

I watched until thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days sat down. His clothing was white as snow; the hair of his head was like pure wool; his throne was like a flame of fire, and its wheels were burning like fire.
A river of fire was flowing before him; thousands upon thousands served him, and myriads upon myriads stood before him. The court sat, and the books were opened.
I watched then, because of the sound of the great words that the horn was speaking, how the beast was slain and perished, and its body was given to the fire to be burned.
And dominion was taken away from the rest of the beasts, but a prolonging of life was given to them for a time.
I was watching in the vision of the night, and behold, on the clouds of heaven one like a son of man was coming, and he came to the Ancient of Days and was presented before him.

And to him were given dominion and honor and kingship, and all peoples, tribes, and languages served him. His authority is an everlasting authority that will not pass away, and his kingdom will not be destroyed.
My heart trembled within my body, and the vision of my head alarmed me, Daniel.
And I approached one of those who were standing there, and I sought to learn from him exactly about all this. He told me plainly, made known to me the interpretation of the words, and said:
"These four beasts are four kings who will arise on the earth, who will be taken away,
and the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom, and will possess it forever, to the ages of ages."

And I sought to know the truth about the fourth beast, for it was greater than the others and exceedingly terrible. Its teeth were of iron and its claws of bronze; it devoured and crushed to pieces, and trampled the remainder with its feet.

And about the ten horns that were on its head, and about the one horn that came up last and uprooted the first three, the horn whose eyes and mouth spoke great things, and whose appearance was greater than all those other beasts.
I was watching, and that horn made war with the saints and grew strong against them,
until the Ancient of Days came, and judgment was given to the saints of the Most High, and the time arrived, and the saints took possession of the kingdom.
And he said: That fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom on the earth, which will surpass all the kingdoms. It will devour the whole earth, trample it down, and crush it.
And its ten horns are ten kings who will arise, and after them another will arise, who will surpass in wickedness all who were before him, and he will bring low three kings.

And he will speak words against the Most High, and he will make war on the saints of the Most High, and he will think to change times and law. And it will be given into his hands for times and times and part of a time.
And they held council and considered, so that they might take away the dominion, to destroy it and to annihilate it completely.

And the reign and the authority and the wealth of the kingdoms under the whole heaven were given to the saints of the Most High. His reign is an everlasting reign, and all dominions and authorities will serve him. Here is the end of the words.
As for me, Daniel, my thoughts troubled me greatly, and the color of my face changed, and I kept the matter hidden in my heart.
In the third year of King Belshazzar a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after my first vision.
I was in the fortress of Susa, which is in the land of Elam, and I was standing by the Ulai.
And I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, a ram was standing by the Ulai. It had high horns, and one was higher than the other, and the higher one came up last.
And I saw the ram butting toward the west, the north, and the south. No beasts could stand before it, and there was no one to rescue from its hand. It did as it pleased and became great.
And as I was pondering, behold, a male goat was coming from the southwest across the face of the whole earth, and it did not touch the ground. And the goat had a horn between its eyes.
And it came right up to the ram that had the horns, which I had seen standing before the Ulai, and it charged at it in the fury of its strength.

And I saw it come right up to the ram. It was enraged against it, and it struck the ram and broke its two horns, and the ram had no strength to stand before it. It threw the ram to the ground and trampled it, and there was no one to rescue the ram from its hand.
And the male goat became exceedingly great. But at the height of its strength its great horn was broken, and four horns came up beneath it, toward the four winds of heaven.
And from one of them came out one small horn, and it grew exceedingly great toward the south and toward the host.
It grew great as far as the host of heaven, and some of that host and of the stars fell down to the earth, and it trampled them,
until the chief commander rescues the captives. And because of him they will take away the sacrifice. And it acted and prospered, and the sanctuary will be made desolate.
And sin was laid upon the sacrifice, and righteousness fell to the ground; and it acted, and it prospered.

And I heard the voice of a holy one speaking, and one holy one said to Pelmoni, the one who was speaking: "How long will this vision last, and this sacrifice that was taken away, and the sin of desolation that was set up, and the holy place and the host be trampled down?"
And he said to him: "Until evening and morning, two thousand three hundred days; and the sanctuary will be cleansed."
And while I, Daniel, was seeing the vision, I was seeking to understand it; and behold, there stood before me something like the appearance of a man.
And I heard a man's voice between the banks of the Ulai, and it said: "Gabriel, make this man understand the vision."
And he came and stood near where I was standing, and when he came I was terrified and fell on my face. And he said to me: "Understand, son of man, for this vision is for the end."
And while he was speaking to me I fainted, and I fell on my face to the ground; and he touched me and set me on my feet.
And he said to me: "Behold, I will make known to you what will happen at the last wrath, for there is a set time until the end.
The ram that you saw, which had horns, is the king of the Persians and the Medes.
And the he-goat is the king of the Greeks, and the great horn that was between its eyes is the first king,
which was broken, and in whose place four horns arose: four kings will arise from his nation, but not with his power.
And at the latter end of their kingdom, when their sins have reached their full measure, a king will arise, shameless of face and understanding riddles.
And his power will be strong, but not by his own power; and he will destroy wonderfully, and he will prosper and act, and he will destroy the mighty and the holy people.

And the yoke of his hand will prosper; deceit will be in his hands, and his heart will be lifted up, and by deceit he will destroy many, and he will rise up to bring many to ruin, and he will crush them by hand like eggs.
And the vision of the evening and the morning that was told is true. And you, seal up the vision, for it is for many days to come."
And I, Daniel, fell sick and lay down, and afterwards I got up and went about the king's business. And I was astonished at the vision, and there was no one who understood it.
In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, of the race of the Medes, who reigned over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,
I, Daniel, understood from the books the number of the years, according to the word of the Lord to Jeremiah the prophet, until the desolation of Jerusalem would be complete: seventy years.
And I turned my face to the Lord to seek him by prayer and supplication, with fasting and sackcloth.
And I prayed to the Lord my God and made confession, and said: "O Lord God, great and wonderful and mighty, who keep the covenant and mercy for those who love you and keep your commandments,
we have sinned; we have become lawless, and have turned away from you, and have turned aside from your commandments and your judgments.
And we did not listen to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings and princes and to all the people of the land.

To you, O Lord, belongs righteousness, and to us the shame of our face, as on this day, to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem and all Israel, those who are near and those who are far off in every land, where you scattered them for their disobedience, because they did not obey you.
O Lord, to us belongs the shame of our face, and to our kings and to our fathers, who sinned against you.
To the Lord our God, yours are mercies and yours are forgivenesses, for we have rebelled against you,
and we did not listen to your voice, O Lord our God, to walk in your laws, which you set before our [?fathers] by the hand of your prophets.

And all Israel transgressed your law and turned aside, so as not to listen to your voice. And the curse came and fell upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses your servant, for we sinned against him.

And he confirmed his words which he spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, by bringing upon us such a very great calamity as had never been anywhere, nor will be under the whole of heaven, like the days that befell Jerusalem.

As it is written in the law of Moses, all this came and fell upon us, and we did not [?] in prayer before the face of the Lord our God, to turn back from our iniquity and to understand all the truth of our Lord.
And the Lord our God kept watch over the calamity against us and sent all this upon us, for the Lord our God is righteous in all his doing which he has done to us, for we did not listen to his voice.
And now, O Lord our God, who brought your people out of the land of the Egyptians with your strong hand, and made yourself a name as at this day: we have sinned; we have become lawless.

O Lord, your mercy is in all things; turn away the anger of your wrath from your city Jerusalem and from your holy mountain, for through our sins and the iniquities of our fathers Jerusalem and your people have been made a reproach among all who were round about us.
And now hear us, O Lord our God, hear the prayer of your servant, and accept his supplications; make your face shine upon your sanctuary, which has been laid waste, for your own sake, O Lord.

Incline your ear, O God, and hear us; open your eyes and see our ruin and that of your city, upon which your name has been laid; for it is not on account of our righteousness that we have set our heart on being accepted, but according to your mercy.
Hear us, O Lord, and forgive our sins; look upon us, O Lord; act, O Lord, and do not delay, for your name's sake, O Lord our God, for your name is laid upon this your city.
While I was still speaking and recounting my sins and the sins of my people Israel, and was only pleading for mercy for myself before the Lord my God, for the holy mountain of the Lord my God,
The words of the prayer were still in my mouth, and behold, I saw the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in my first vision, coming in flight;
and he drew near to me just at the hour of the evening service, and he gave me understanding, and spoke to me and said: "Daniel, now I have come to inform you."

"At the very beginning of your prayers the words went forth from your mouth, and I have come to tell you, for you are a blessed man. Now consider by this word of yours, and take to heart this vision which you have seen:

Seventy weeks have been appointed upon your people and upon your holy city, until they grow old, to complete sins, and to seal them, and to blot out lawlessness, and to relieve [?] falsehoods, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal visions and prophecies, and to anoint the Holy of Holies.

And know and understand: from the going forth of the word to answer and to rebuild Jerusalem until Christ the leader there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks; and he will restore it, and will rebuild the streets and the wall, and the times will be renewed.

And after the sixty-two weeks the anointing will be destroyed, and there will be no judgment in it and in the city; and they will also destroy the sanctuary together with the ruler who is coming, and they will be cut off by upheaval [?], until the end of a shortened war and of destruction.

And he will make the covenant strong for many for one week, and in half of the week he will take away sacrifice and offering, and in the temple there will be the abomination of desolation, and until the completion of the time an end will be given to the desolation."
In the third year of Cyrus king of the Persians a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, and the word is true; and great power and understanding were given to him in that vision.
In those days I, Daniel, was in mourning for three weeks of days.
I ate no desirable bread, and neither meat nor wine entered my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with ointment until the three weeks of days were completed.
On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, in the third year, I had come and was standing by the great river, that is, the Tigris, Hiddekel.
And I lifted up my eyes and looked; and behold, a man clothed in linen, and his loins girded with gold of Uphaz.

And his body was shining and pure, and his face was like the appearance of lightning, and his eyes like torches of fire, and his arms and his legs like gleaming bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a great multitude.
And I, Daniel, alone saw this vision, and those who were with me did not see the vision; but great amazement fell upon them, and they fled in fear.
And I was left alone, and I saw this great apparition, and no strength remained in me, and my glory was turned into corruption, and no strength stayed with me.
And I heard the sound of his words, and as I heard them I became sorrowful, and my face was bowed to the ground.
And behold, a hand which touched me, and raised me up upon my knees,

and he said to me: "Daniel, man greatly desired, understand the words which I speak to you, and stand in your place, for I have been sent to you." And as he was speaking these words to me, I stood up trembling,

And he said to me: "Do not be afraid, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before God, your words were heard, and I have come because of your words.

And the prince of the kingdom of the Persians stood against me for twenty-one days, and behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I left him there with the prince of the kingdom of the Persians.
And I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people in the last days, for this vision is for those [?] days."
And when he spoke these words to me, I turned my face to the ground.

And behold, one in the likeness of a son of man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and spoke, and I said to the one standing before me: "Lord, at your vision my insides were turned within me, and I had no strength left.
And how can your servant stand and speak with this lord of mine? From now on no strength remains in me, and no breath is left in me."
And again one with the appearance of a man touched me, and strengthened me.
And he said to me: "Do not be afraid, greatly beloved man. Peace be with you. Be courageous and be strong." And as the angel spoke to me, I was strengthened, and I said:

"Let my lord speak, for he has strengthened me." And he said to me: "Do you know why I have come to you? And now I will return to fight with the prince of the Persians; and as I was going out, the prince of the Greeks was coming.
But I will tell you what is written in the book of truth. And there is no one who helps me against them except Michael, your prince.
And in the first year of Cyrus I stood up as strength and support.

And now I will tell you the truth. Behold, three [?] kings will arise in Persia, and the fourth will become rich with great wealth, more than all of them, and after he has gained that wealth he will rise up against all the kings of the Greeks.
And another king will arise, a mighty one, and he will rule with great dominion and do as he pleases.

And as soon as his kingdom is established, it will be broken and divided toward the four winds of heaven, but not to his descendants. His end will not match the power with which he ruled, for his kingdom will be uprooted and given to others besides these [?].
And the king of the south will grow strong, but one of his princes will grow stronger than him and will rule with great dominion.

And after his years they will make an alliance, and the daughter of the king of the south will go in; she will come to the king of the north to make an agreement with him. But she will not keep the strength of her arm, and his offspring will not endure. And the woman will be handed over, together with those who brought her, the young girl, and the one who supported her in those times.
One will arise from a shoot of her root, in his prepared [place] [?], and he will come against the army and enter the strongholds of the king of the north, and he will act against them and prevail.
And their gods too, along with their molten images, and all their precious vessels, and gold and silver, they will carry off as plunder to Egypt; and he will stand over the king of the north.
And he will enter the kingdom of the king of the south, and then return to his own land.
And his sons will gather a great assembly of a mighty host. He will surely come and sweep through and come on, and he will settle down as far as his stronghold.
And the king of the south will be enraged. He will come out and fight against the king of the north, and he will raise a great host, and that host will be given into his hand.
And he will carry that host away, and his heart will be lifted up to cast down tens of thousands, but he will not prevail.
And the king of the north will return and bring a host greater than the first. At the end of the times and years he will surely come in with a great army and much wealth.
And in those times many will rise up against the king of the south, and the vile sons of your people will exalt themselves to fulfil the vision, and they will fail.

And the king of the north will come in and set up a [?] (siege mound?), and he will seize strong cities. The arms of the king of the south will not withstand him, nor his chosen men, and there will be no strength to withstand.
And the one who comes in against him will do as he wills, and there is no one who can stand before him. He will remain in the land of Sabir, and it will be consumed by his hand.

And he will set his face to come in with the strength of his whole kingdom, and he will make a full agreement with him. He will give him a daughter of women in order to destroy it, but it will not stand, nor will it be his.
And he will turn his face to the coastlands and seize many cities. He will make rulers cease from their reproach, but his own reproach will turn back upon him.
And he will turn his face toward the strongholds of his own land, and he will grow weak and fall.
And in his place one will arise who carries off the glory of the kingdom, and in those days he will be broken, neither by anger nor by battle.
In his place will arise one who is despised, and the glory of the kingdom will not be given to him. He will come in prosperity and strengthen his kingdom by [?] (seizures?).
And the arms of the one who sweeps away will be swept away before him and broken, and also the leader of the covenant.
From among those allied [?] he will practise deceit toward him. He will come up and become stronger than him with a small people.

He will come with wealth and into the richest regions, and he will do what his fathers and his fathers' fathers did not do: plunder and spoil and wealth he will share out among them. He will devise plans against Egypt, but only for a time.

And his strength and his heart will be stirred up against the king of the south with a great army. The king of the south will wage war with a very strong army, but he will not stand, for they will devise plans against him.
And they will eat his food and break him, and his forces will be swept away, and many will fall slain.
And the hearts of both kings will be set on evil. They will speak lies at one table, but it will not succeed, for the end is still to come at the appointed time.
And he will return to his own land with much wealth, and his heart will be set against the holy covenant. He will act, and return to his own land.
At the appointed time he will return and come into the south, but the latter will not be like the former.

And the Kittim who go forth will come in that year [?], and he will be humbled and turn back. He will rage against the holy law and act, and he will return and give heed to those who forsook the holy law.
And offspring from him will arise. They will defile the sanctuary of strength, remove the service of the sacrifices, and set up the defiling abomination.
And those who have become lawless will bring a stumbling block upon the law. They will speak vain things, but the people who know their God will prevail over them and will act.
And those of your people who have understanding will give understanding in all things. They will be weakened by the sword, by the flame of fire, by captivity and by plunder for days.
And in their weakness they will receive help, a little help, and many will join them in deceit.
And some of those who have understanding will be weakened so that they may be refined by fire, wait, and be revealed until the time of the end, because it is still for an appointed time.

And the king will do as he wills. He will exalt himself and magnify himself above every god. He will speak outrageous things, and he will prosper until the wrath is accomplished, because it is at the end.
And he will pay no heed to any of the gods of his fathers, nor to the desire of women. He will pay no heed to any gods, because he will magnify himself above all.
And in his place he will glorify the god Maozim. He will also glorify a god whom his fathers did not know, with silver and gold, precious stone and desirable things.
And he will make the strongholds a refuge for those who flee to a foreign god, and he will increase glory. He will subject many to himself, and he will divide the land with gifts.
And at the time of the end the king of the south will butt at him. The king of the north will gather against him with chariots, horsemen and many ships.
And he will enter the land and crush it, and he will pass through the land of Sabir, and many will be weakened. But these will escape from his hand: Edom, Moab and the rulers of the sons of Ammon.
And he will stretch out his hand over the land, and the land of Egypt will not be a place of safety.
And he will rule over the hidden treasures of gold and silver and over all the desirable things of Egypt, of the Libyans and of the Ethiopians, and over their fortified places.
And reports and haste will alarm him from the east and from the north, and he will come with great wrath to destroy many.
And he will pitch his tent at the baths [?] between the two seas, at the holy mountain Sabir. He will come as far as his portion [?], and there will be no one else to deliver him.

And at that time Michael will arise, the great prince who stands over the sons of your people. There will be a time of distress, such distress as has not been from the time a nation came into being until that time. At that time your people will be delivered, everyone who is found written in the book of life.
And many who were sleeping in the dust of the earth will arise, some to everlasting life and some to everlasting reproach and shame.
And those who have understanding will shine like the brightness of the firmament, and many of the righteous will shine like the stars of heaven for ever and beyond.
And you, Daniel, shut up these words and seal the book until the time of the end, until many are taught and knowledge increases.
And I, Daniel, looked, and two others were standing, one on this bank of the river and one on the other bank.
And they said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river: "How long until the end of these wonders that you have spoken of?"

And I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the water of the river. He raised his right hand and his left hand to heaven and swore by the One who lives forever that it would be for a time, times and part of a time; at the completion of the scattering they will know all these things.
And I heard and understood, and I said: "Lord, what will the end of these things be for me, and what is their explanation?"
"Come, Daniel, for the words are closed up and sealed until the time of the end.
Until then many will be chosen, made white and refined by fire. The lawless will act lawlessly and will not understand, but those who have knowledge will understand.
From the time when the perpetual service is changed and the abomination of desolation is set up, there will be one thousand two hundred and ninety days.
Blessed is the one who reaches and endures to the one thousand three hundred and thirty-fifth day.
And you, come and take your rest. There are still days until the end is fulfilled. You will rest, and you will rise to your portion at the end of the days."
